title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 101
paragraphs: On hearing this, Xerxes was as rejoiced and delighted as he could be after his misfortunes, and he told Mardonius that when he had taken counsel he would reply and say which of these two courses he would follow. So when he was taking counsel with those Persians summoned to advise him, it seemed good to him to send for Artemisia too, because she alone on the former occasion had shown perception of what ought to be done. When Artemisia arrived, Xerxes removed everyone else — both the Persian councillors and the spearmen of the guard — and spoke to her thus: “Mardonius bids me stay here and make an attempt on the Peloponnese, saying that the Persians and the land-army are in no way to blame for my calamity, and that they would gladly give me proof of this. He urges me either to do this, or else he himself offers to choose three hundred thousand from the army and deliver over to me Greece reduced to subjection, while I withdraw with the rest of the army to my own home. Since you counseled well about the sea-battle that was fought — urging that we should not bring it on — advise me now too which of these things I should do, so that I may succeed in deciding well.”
